evidence.title: Kong Dan
evidence.text: Kong Dan (Simplified Chinese: 孔丹) (born 1947 in Beijing, China with family roots in Pingxiang, Jiangxi, China) is a Chinese entrepreneur and economist.

evidence.title: Kong Dan
evidence.text: He is the chairman of the CITIC Group.

evidence.title: Kong Dan
evidence.text: He is also the chairman of CITIC International Financial Holdings, China CITIC Bank and CITIC Resources Holdings.

evidence.title: China CITIC Bank
evidence.text: China CITIC Bank () is China’s seventh-largest lender in terms of total assets.

evidence.title: China CITIC Bank
evidence.text: It was known as CITIC Industrial Bank until it changed its name in August 2005.

evidence.title: China CITIC Bank
evidence.text: China CITIC Bank, established in 1987, is a nationally comprehensive and internationally oriented commercial bank.

evidence.title: China CITIC Bank
evidence.text: The bank operates in almost 130 countries, and maintains a strong foothold on the mainland banking industry.

evidence.title: China CITIC Bank
evidence.text: The bank operates 78 branches in the mainland, and 622 sub-branches, located in economically developed regions of China.

evidence.title: China CITIC Bank
evidence.text: In total, there are 773 branch offices in China, as of Q4 2011.

evidence.title: UniCredit Bank Slovakia
evidence.text: UniCredit Bank Slovakia was a Slovak bank, formed by the merger of HVB Bank Slovakia and UniBanka in 2007, both owned by Italy-based UniCredit Group.

evidence.title: UniCredit Bank Slovakia
evidence.text: In 2013 it was absorbed by UniCredit Bank Czech Republic, forming UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia.

evidence.title: Ka Wah Bank
evidence.text: Ka Wah Bank Limited (Traditional Chinese: 嘉華銀行有限公司) (Former stock code: ) was a bank in Hong Kong.

evidence.title: Ka Wah Bank
evidence.text: It was acquired by CITIC International Financial Holdings and renamed as CITIC Ka Wah Bank Limited (Traditional Chinese: 中信嘉華銀行有限公司)(In May 2010, CITIC Ka Wah Bank Limited was renamed as CITIC Bank International Limited(Traditional Chinese: 中信銀行國際有限公司)).

evidence.title: China Investment Bank
evidence.text: China Investment Bank () was a defunct bank of China.

evidence.title: China Investment Bank
evidence.text: It was became a subsidiary of China Construction Bank in 1994.

evidence.title: China Investment Bank
evidence.text: In 1998 it was absorbed by China Development Bank, with some business was received by China CITIC Bank.

evidence.title: UniCredit
evidence.text: UniCredit S.p.A. is an Italian global banking and financial services company.

evidence.title: UniCredit
evidence.text: Its network spans 50 markets in 17 countries, with more than 8,500 branches and over 147,000 employees.

evidence.title: UniCredit
evidence.text: Its strategic position in Western and Eastern Europe gives the group one of the region's highest market shares.

evidence.title: UniCredit
evidence.text: The company is a component of the Euro Stoxx 50 stock market index.

evidence.title: Zhong Tian Plaza
evidence.text: China CITIC Bank Mansion (), formerly Zhong Tian Plaza () is a 59-floor/229-meter tall skyscraper in Urumqi, Xinjiang, People's Republic of China.

evidence.title: Zhong Tian Plaza
evidence.text: It is the tallest building in Northwestern China and Central Asia.

evidence.title: Bank Austria
evidence.text: UniCredit Bank Austria AG, better known as Bank Austria, is an Austria bank, 96.35% owned by UniCredit Group.

evidence.title: Bank Austria
evidence.text: The bank maintains an extensive network in Austria, with about 7,700 employees serving customers in some 300 branches.

evidence.title: Bank Austria
evidence.text: Bank Austria also served as UniCredit's intermediate holding company for the banking network in Central and Eastern Europe (until September 2016), a region where the Group is the clear market leader with about 3,900 branches in 19 countries.

evidence.title: Bank Austria
evidence.text: However, all the CEE subsidiaries were transferred to the parent company in September 2016.

evidence.title: Bank Austria
evidence.text: As per 2008, 85% of Bank Austria's total workforce is employed out of Austria.

evidence.title: CITIC Publishing Group
evidence.text: CITIC Publishing Group () is a publishing company under CITIC Group based in Beijing, China.

evidence.title: CITIC Publishing Group
evidence.text: It was established on in 1988 as China CITIC Press and was reorganized to CITIC Publishing Group in 2008.

evidence.title: CITIC Bank International
evidence.text: CITIC Bank International () (Former stock code: ) ("formerly" known as CITIC Ka Wah Bank () and Ka Wah Bank) is a Hong Kong bank majority owned by CITIC.

evidence.title: CITIC Bank International
evidence.text: It is a subsidiary of CITIC International Financial Holdings.
